title: Shanghai’s ‘Meilong San Cun’ Community: The Successful Transformation of a ‘Garbage Village’ Through Low-Carbon Innovative Practices
summary: This C40 case study describes “Shanghai’s ‘Meilong San Cun’ Community: The Successful Transformation of a ‘Garbage Village’ Through Low-Carbon Innovative Practices,” an urban initiative documented for Shanghai. It is included because it is located in the Global South. intervention.objectives: Built in 1990, Meilong San Cun is a typical public housing community of Shanghai, counting 2,369 households with a population of about 6,500, with majority of relocated households. Meilong Cun’s “green culture” developed as the community turned from a “garbage village” to a “clean community” and then to a “low-carbon community”, largely thanks to the success of the “ Green Housewives ” volunteer movement (retired community residents that volunteer to promote green culture in the community and promote sustainable practices from waste management to green spaces management).
